title: Foundations of Writing
full_title: Foundations of Writing: Observation, Narrative and Description
tagline: The writing process, observation and material, theme and structure, narration, description, expressing feeling, exposition, language and punctuation, and revision
summary: Most school leavers have written hundreds of compositions to a formula; good writing starts from looking closely and saying exactly what you mean. This course covers the writing process from observation and gathering material to choosing a theme and a structure, the modes of narration, description, expression of feeling and exposition, clear and correct language including punctuation, and the habit of revision.
overview: Almost everyone has written hundreds of school compositions; almost no one was taught writing as a process rather than a product. This course rebuilds the fundamentals from the ground up: learning to see, then learning to say — observation notebooks, a single controlling theme, narration's chronology and its deviations, description's five senses, exposition's cold clarity, and the unglamorous craft of revision.

It takes Chinese school writing seriously and asks it to be less formulaic: 套路 — opening with “as the ancients said”, closing with “I aspire”—is treated as what it is: a default that outsources thinking. Chinese models carry the teaching line (the Ye Shengtao, Xia Minzun school), while the workshop science is imported: process writing, Flower & Hayes' cognitive model, Peter Elbow's free-writing — shelves Chinese classrooms deserve and increasingly use.
Prerequisites: none — this is a “from zero to a submittable draft” course; the rhetoric and grammar courses run parallel and will show up whenever you need them.
outcomes: run the full writing process (accumulate—conceive—draft—revise—proofread) on a 1,000-word piece under time constraints
keep an observation notebook that distinguishes seeing, inferring, and feeling, and mine it for material
reduce a composition to one controlling theme and prune every sentence that serves another master
order a narrative deliberately (顺叙/倒叙/插叙) with six-element bookkeeping and scene-vs-summary proportioning
write description that uses all five senses, fixed and moving viewpoints, and 白描 vs 工笔 as strategy
choose exposition modes (definition, division, examples, comparison, sequence) to match reader and purpose
revise at three levels — structural, paragraph, sentence — and proofread by typesetting-error class (错字、别字、漏字、标点)
diagnose and remove 套话 (formulaic diction): fake citations, aspiration-endings, and the counterfeit 深情 of stock emotion

chapters.title: The writing process
chapters.summary: From the urge to write to a finished piece: gathering, planning, drafting and revising, and why formulaic exam compositions are a poor model.

chapters.title: Observation and material
chapters.summary: Seeing and recording precisely, keeping notebooks, reading as a writer, and choosing material.

chapters.title: Theme and structure
chapters.summary: Finding what a piece is about, openings and endings, transitions and echoes, and the shape of the whole.

chapters.title: Narration
chapters.summary: Telling events clearly: order, person and point of view, pace, and detail.

chapters.title: Description
chapters.summary: Describing people, places and scenes through the senses, and the difference between description and decoration.

chapters.title: Expressing feeling
chapters.summary: Direct and indirect expression of feeling, feeling conveyed through scene and event, and restraint.

chapters.title: Exposition
chapters.summary: Explaining things and processes clearly: definition, classification, example, comparison and figures.

chapters.title: Language and punctuation
chapters.summary: Plain, precise language, the national standards for punctuation (GB/T 15834—2011) and for numbers (GB/T 15835—2011), and common errors.

chapters.title: Revision
chapters.summary: Revising for content, structure and language, reading aloud to check, and giving and using feedback.

history.title: Composition enters the timetable
history.detail: The 癸卯–壬寅 school regulations make 中国文学/作文 a standing subject with graded exercises (monthly 课作, term 季考) — classroom writing in China begins as homework with a schedule.

history.title: Vernacular gets the green light
history.detail: The Ministry of Education orders vernacular (语体) in primary reading texts; children may now write as they speak — the century's greatest upgrade (and downgrade) of the composition assignment.

history.title: The first composition-method textbooks
history.detail: Mid-1920s Chengda-school 作文范本 appear (后由叶圣陶等修订推行), and 叶圣陶、夏丏尊的《文心》式读写教材继之 — writing pedagogy becomes a book trade with classics.

history.title: The “double basics” line
history.detail: The first national 中学语文教学大纲 stresses 基础知识和基本技能 (later canonized as “双基”) — composition drills get a syllabus; 套路化 gets its institutional excuse.

history.title: The essay returns to the exam hall
history.detail: With the gaokao restored, 作文 reappears as a scored section after a decade's absence — an entire generation learns to write again at night, copying 范文 with 红笔批改.

history.title: Writing as a cognitive process
history.detail: Flower & Hayes publish their planning–translating–reviewing model; “process writing” (预写—起草—修改—校对) reshapes composition teaching worldwide, China's imported wing included.

history.title: The Standards de-formulaize
history.detail: The new 全日制义务教育语文课程标准 asks for 有创意地表达 and cuts the topic-essay farce — 不限文体、贴近生活; the 套路 fights back by teaching “innovative” templates.

history.title: A letter becomes a national argument
history.detail: A gaokao task asks candidates to write a letter to a relative who phoned while driving; the “老张” essays flood media and re-ask the century-old question: can honest writing be assessed, or only honest-sounding writing?

references.title: 《文心》
references.note: Stories teaching reading-and-writing — the Chinese standard for “textbook you actually want to read.”

references.title: Writing Without Teachers
references.note: Free-writing and the belief that messy first drafts are the method, not the failure — 自由写作法之源。

references.title: A Cognitive Process Theory of Writing
references.note: The process model's founding paper: planning, translating, reviewing — writing as observable cognition.

references.title: On Writing Well
references.note: The English nonfiction tradition's clearest sermon on clutter — a useful mirror for 中文“简洁”训练。

references.title: 《综合高中语文》（实验课本）
references.note: The controversial integrated Chinese textbook (读史、读文、说与写、想想) — a case study in how composition reform gets fought.
